chunks: Ibn Mahbub narrated from Ali ibn Ri'ab, who said:

I heard Aba Abdillah عليه السلام say: “It is not proper for a man among you to enter into partnership with a dhimmi, nor to entrust him with merchandise, nor to deposit a trust with him, nor to establish sincere affection with him.”

key_terms.وَدِيعَةً: a deposited trust or property left in someone’s care
key_terms.يُبْضِعَهُ: to consign or entrust merchandise to someone for trade
key_terms.يُشَارِكَ: to enter into a business partnership with
key_terms.ٱلذِّمِّيَّ: a non-Muslim living under Muslim protection and covenant

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about partnership and close relations with a dhimmi?
ai.summary: This hadith conveys a ruling and ethical caution regarding certain forms of close financial and personal association with a dhimmi. It addresses partnership, entrusting goods, depositing property, and intimate affection, reflecting boundaries in social and commercial dealings.
